subject: GPU backpressure observed on Dedicated pool — SLA exception & mitigation steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@brightwave.ai>, BrightWave Ops <ops@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: GPU backpressure observed on your Dedicated pool — initial update

Hi Elena / BrightWave Ops team,

I wanted to alert you that at ~07:43 PST we started observing persistent backpressure on your Dedicated GPU pool (pool-id: bw-prod-3). This manifested as increased request queueing and token-latency spikes for ~20 minutes, driven by a burst in long-sequence generation requests from two internal workflows.

Immediate actions we took:  
- Routed new requests to your configured fallback model variant (gpt-large-quant) to preserve latency SLOs.
- Temporarily increased autoscaling aggressiveness for the pool (2->4 warm nodes) to relieve queueing.
- Collected KV cache and utilization snapshots; attached the CSV for your review.

Impact: Some requests experienced 4–9s tail latency; throughput hit the committed throughput floor for ~15 minutes. No data exfiltration or authorization failures.

We're continuing to monitor. Marissa and Jonas are triaging root cause and will propose a mitigation timeline. Can you confirm if you saw errors from the BrightWave side (timeouts/retries) and whether you want us to initiate a manual capacity bump while we complete the follow-up?

I'll schedule a short call in the next hour if helpful.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attach: utilization_snapshot_20261130.csv
From: Elena Soto <elena@brightwave.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightWave Ops <ops@brightwave.ai>, Chris Tanner <chris.tanner@brightwave.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:28:14 -0800
Subject: Re: GPU backpressure observed on your Dedicated pool — initial update

Thanks Kimberly — we did see an uptick in 5xx and a handful of client retries between 07:40–07:55. Most user-facing workflows degraded (not full outages) but our ingestion pipeline retried aggressively which amplified the load.

Two asks from BrightWave:  
1) If you can open a formal SLA exception for the window and advise on credits we should expect, that helps our finance team.
2) We'd like a short postmortem with root cause and clear mitigation so we can update our on-call runbooks.

Call is fine; we're available at 09:00 PST.

—Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightWave Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@brightwave.ai>, BrightWave Ops <ops@brightwave.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GPU backpressure observed on your Dedicated pool — follow-up plan and credit proposal

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick confirmation and availability. We joined the 09:00 PST call and captured actions; summarizing here for the thread and for your finance team.

Root cause (preliminary):  
- A spike of long-context generation jobs from a BrightWave batch (ingestion retry loop) caused sustained sequence lengths above the pool's usual distribution.
- The serving runtime prioritized throughput which led to headroom exhaustion for low-latency routing and increased queueing.

Mitigation completed during incident:  
- Forced teardown of two overloaded worker instances and redeployed with adjusted kernel selection to favor lower memory usage.
- Enabled per-request priority routing for low-latency calls and diverted background batch jobs to a delayed queue.
- Increased autoscale target temporarily (as Kimberly noted).

Planned next steps (72h):  
1) Postmortem doc with timeline, root cause confirmation, and regression tests (owner: Jonas). Estimated draft: 2026-12-02.
2) Config change to the Dedicated pool to enforce per-tenant sequence-length caps and a background-job backoff policy (owner: Marissa). Rollout window: 12/03–12/04 off-peak.
3) Add a conservative autoscale ramp profile for BrightWave that triggers earlier on queue depth (owner: Lauren).

SLA credit proposal: Redwood proposes a one-time credit equal to 7 days of Dedicated base subscription prorated to your committed nodes (deal DW-4821). If that is acceptable we will issue the credit to your billing contact.

Attachments: redwood_mitigation_plan.pdf (mitigation steps + rollout calendar)

If that all looks good we'll move to schedule the postmortem and the config rollout.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GPU backpressure observed on your Dedicated pool — confirmation & next steps

Elena — thanks again for taking the call and confirming impacts. Confirming next steps from Redwood's side:  
- We'll publish the incident postmortem (draft by 2026-12-02) and a final postmortem after the rollout.
- The proposed credit (7 days prorated) will be applied to your account and you will receive a formal billing note within 3 business days.
- Change window for per-tenant caps / backoff policy scheduled 2026-12-03 02:00–04:00 PST (low traffic). We'll send a reminder 48h prior and a 1h pre-notice.

If BrightWave wants a dry-run of the cap behavior we can run a controlled replay in a sandbox next week; Jonas can coordinate.

Appended: brief attachment summaries and links to the incident runbook.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
